purpose: Registers filesystem `path` data on the wppo-combine-css handle so WordPress core's wp_maybe_inline_styles() inlines the combined/minified CSS (within the styles_inline_size_limit budget) instead of emitting a render-blocking link, with a used-CSS conflict gate and an opt-out filter, and suppresses the preload hint when inlining applies.
riskRationale: The inlining mechanism is sound: the hook-ordering premise was verified against core default-filters.php, the removeUnusedCSS conflict gate is genuinely necessary, and the opt-out filter follows plugin conventions. However, the PR also commits ~4,737 dev-only vendor files (~525K lines) into the tracked production-only vendor directory, and the preload-suppression logic can drop the preload for files core will not inline (20-40KB files on WP < 6.9 due to a hardcoded 40000-byte default, and any file when other queued styles consume core's cumulative budget). Inlined CSS is also baked into every cached static HTML page, contradicting the PR's repeat-visit external-file claim. No security or crash risk.
breakingChanges: On WP 6.2-6.8, combined CSS files sized ~20-40KB lose their <link rel=preload> hint without being inlined (previous behavior always preloaded).
Inlined CSS is baked into every cached static HTML page, so repeat visitors re-download the CSS bytes in HTML instead of reusing the browser-cached external file.
The tracked repository footprint grows by ~4,737 dev-only vendor files / ~525K lines.

text: The class-cache.php change is well-researched and mostly correct: it uses core's canonical wp_maybe_inline_styles() opt-in, the hook-ordering premise was verified, the removeUnusedCSS conflict gate is necessary, and the wppo_inline_combined_css filter is a clean escape hatch. Two issues must be resolved before merge: the preload-suppression size gate hardcodes the WP 6.9+ 40000-byte default (core uses 20000 on WP < 6.9 and applies a cumulative queue budget), regressing preloads for files core will not inline, and the commit accidentally ships the entire dev-dependency vendor tree (~4,737 files) against the documented composer release convention. The repeat-visit inlining behavior also contradicts the PR description and needs documenting or a deliberate product decision.

reasoning: Blocking: (1) the preload-suppression check hardcodes 40000 bytes while core's styles_inline_size_limit default is 20000 on WP < 6.9 and is cumulative across all path-registered styles, so preloads are dropped for files core will never inline; (2) ~4,737 dev-only vendor files were committed contrary to the production-only vendor convention. The always-inline behavior must also be corrected or documented before merge.

message: The removeUnusedCSS conflict gate is correct and necessary: core's wp_maybe_inline_styles() sets src to false on inlined handles, and Used_CSS::get_all_css_assets() reads CSS content through $wp_styles->registered[handle]->src and silently skips empty src values - without this guard, used-CSS regeneration would ship the full unpurged CSS.

The hook-ordering premise is accurate and was verified against core default-filters.php: wp_enqueue_scripts is registered on wp_head priority 1 before wp_maybe_inline_styles (same priority), and combine_css() runs at wp_enqueue_scripts priority PHP_INT_MAX, so the combined handle with its path data is always in the queue before core evaluates inlining.

The wppo_inline_combined_css opt-out filter is a clean, additive escape hatch for site operators, and the function_exists('wp_maybe_inline_styles') defensive guard correctly keeps the feature inert on older WP versions.

The path data is domain-scoped and matches the enqueued URL (get_cache_file_path()/get_cache_file_url() build identical domain+url_path structures), keeping multisite safe, and both the fresh-cache reuse and new-generation branches register path data symmetrically.

The PR commit (04b05add) adds ~4,737 dev-only dependency files (~525K lines: phpunit, brain/monkey, antecedent/patchwork, mockery, hamcrest, sebastian/*, nikic/php-parser, squizlabs/phpcs, wp-coding-standards/wpcs, etc.) into the tracked vendor/ tree and flips the composer metadata to dev: true. This violates AGENTS.md, which requires committing a production-only vendor produced by `composer release` (composer install --no-dev). The release ZIP is currently only protected because release.yml re-runs composer install --no-dev; .distignore excludes only a handful of dev dirs, so any packaging path that skips that step would ship PHPUnit/PHPCS in the WordPress.org release.
suggestion: Regenerate the committed vendor in production mode: run `composer release` (composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader --ignore-platform-reqs), verify only production deps (voku/html-min, matthiasmullie/minify, woocommerce/action-scheduler) remain, and re-commit vendor/ alongside the class-cache.php change. Consider adding the remaining dev-only dirs to .distignore as defense-in-depth.
suggestionCode:
composer release
git add vendor/
git commit --amend

message: The preload-suppression check hardcodes 40000 as the styles_inline_size_limit default, but core's actual default is 20000 bytes on WP 6.2-6.8 (raised to 40000 only in WP 6.9). Because no callback is hooked, this apply_filters call returns the plugin's own default. On WP < 6.9 a combined CSS file between 20KB and 40KB gets its preload suppressed yet is NOT inlined by core (20KB budget) - a render-blocking stylesheet with no preload, an LCP regression versus the pre-PR behavior that always emitted the preload.
suggestion: Derive the default from the running WP version so the suppression decision matches core's budget.

message: Core's wp_maybe_inline_styles() applies the budget cumulatively: it collects ALL queued styles carrying path data, sorts them by size ascending, and inlines smallest-first until the running total exceeds the limit. The plugin's per-file size check ignores other inlinable styles (core-registered global/block styles, other plugins' path opt-ins) that can consume the budget first, so the combined file - typically the largest - may be skipped even when under the limit while its preload was already suppressed.
suggestion: Only suppress the preload when the combined handle is the sole queued style with path data (or otherwise when inlining is certain); otherwise keep the preload, since a redundant preload is harmless while a missing preload on a non-inlined stylesheet is a regression.

message: The PR description and docblock claim the external file remains on disk for repeat-visit cache hits, but that is not what happens: this plugin's static HTML cache persists the fully rendered output, so the inline <style> produced at generation time is baked into every cached page and served to ALL repeat visitors. The external combined.css is effectively never the repeat-visit asset for eligible files, which loses cross-page browser CSS caching and contradicts the stated design intent.
suggestion: Correct the docblock/PR description to state that inlining is baked into the cached HTML for all visits (with the external file retained only for oversized, used-CSS, or opted-out sites), or gate inlining behind a deliberate policy decision if repeat-visit caching matters.

message: WP_Filesystem::size() returns int|false; if stat fails, false > $limit evaluates to false, so the preload is suppressed while core's wp_filesize() would return 0 and skip inlining (leaving an external link with no preload, and on WP 7.0+ core emits _doing_it_wrong for an unreadable registered path).
suggestion: Cast the size to int before comparing and guard the add_data('path', ...) calls with file_exists()/is_readable() so ineligibility is determined with the same filesystem semantics core uses.

message: `@since 4.1.0` in the new helper's docblock does not match the repo's versioning - the plugin is at 1.8.0 (performance-optimisation.php:8) - and will confuse changelog tooling.
suggestion: Change `@since 4.1.0` to the actual release version this change ships in (e.g. 1.8.0 or the next planned release).

message: No tests were added for the new behavior. should_inline_combined_css() is a pure, unit-testable decision function (removeUnusedCSS branch, function_exists branch, filter branch), and the preload-suppression condition is exactly the kind of version-sensitive logic that warrants regression coverage - particularly the 20KB-vs-40KB default mismatch and the only-path-style check.
suggestion: Add CacheTest cases for should_inline_combined_css() covering: removeUnusedCSS on -> false; wp_maybe_inline_styles missing -> false; filter returning falsy -> false; default -> true; and assert the preload echo is suppressed for a sub-limit file and emitted for an over-limit file.

message: The new wppo_inline_combined_css filter is not documented anywhere (readme, settings screen, or AGENTS.md), making it undiscoverable to site operators who may need to opt out.
suggestion: Document the filter in the readme and/or AGENTS.md so the opt-out is discoverable.
